'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Killing of journalists in the Gaza war]]
***At least eleven [[Palestinians]], including two children and three journalists documenting [[Egypt]]ian state [[Humanitarian aid during the Gaza war|aid distribution]], are killed in [[Israel]]i airstrikes in the [[Netzarim Corridor]] in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. *[[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
**Israel launches a series of [[airstrike]]s in [[Lebanon]], killing one person each in [[Tyre, Lebanon|Tyre]] and [[Sidon]] and wounding 19 others in Qanarit. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1/22/israel-bombs-four-syria-lebanon-border-crossings-kills-2-in-south-lebanon (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
**A [[car bomb]]ing near [[Aden]], [[Yemen]], targeting the motorcade of [[Southern Giants Brigades]] commander Hamdy Shoukry, kills three people and injures four others. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/car-bomb-yemen-kills-3-target-leader-saudi-129419922 (AP via ABC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Orbanomics]], [[Economy of Hungary]]
**[[Hungary|Hungarian]] [[Prime Minister of Hungary|prime minister]] [[Viktor Orbán]] announces a 100-billion-[[Hungarian forint|forint]] ([[United States dollar|US$]]300-million) support package for the [[List of restaurants in Hungary|restaurant sector]] and commits to covering additional household [[Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning|heating]] costs for January, as part of broader measures to ease cost-of-living pressures and revive the economy ahead of the upcoming [[2026 Hungarian parliamentary election|parliamentary elections]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/hungarys-orban-throws-restaurants-304-mln-lifeline-ahead-election-2026-01-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[January 2026 New Zealand storms]]
**[[New Zealand]] [[Territorial authorities of New Zealand|territorial authorities]] order evacuations in [[Flat coast|low-lying]] areas of the [[North Island]] after heavy rain and strong winds cause flooding and landslides, while [[New Zealand Police|police]] search for a man missing after being swept away while [[Ford (crossing)|fording]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/severe-weather-new-zealands-north-island-prompts-evacuations-2026-01-20/ (Reuters)]
*Severe storms in [[Greece]] kill two people as strong winds and heavy rainfall cause flooding, prompting authorities to suspend [[Greek shipping|maritime traffic]] and close schools in several [[Regions of Greece|regions]]. [https://www.bssnews.net/international/353622 (AFP via BSS)]

'''International relations'''
*[[EU–Mercosur Partnership Agreement]]
**The [[European Parliament]] approves a measure by a vote of 334–324 to ask the [[European Court of Justice]] to rule on whether the [[free trade agreement]] between the [[EU]] and [[Mercosur]] can be applied before full [[ratification]] by all [[Member state of the European Union|member states]] and whether its provisions restrict the EU's ability to set [[Environmental policy of the European Union|environmental]] and consumer health policies.  [https://www.reuters.com/world/eu-lawmakers-vote-whether-launch-legal-challenge-mercosur-trade-deal-2026-01-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[Greenland crisis]], [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration]]
**[[United States]] [[President of the United States|president]] [[Donald Trump]] announces he will cancel the planned [[tariff]]s on [[Denmark]], [[Finland]], [[France]], [[Germany]], the [[Netherlands]], [[Norway]], [[Sweden]], and the [[United Kingdom]] after reaching an agreement with [[NATO]] [[Secretary General of NATO|Secretary General]] [[Mark Rutte]] for a [[Greenland]] framework. He also stated at the [[World Economic Forum]] that he has ruled out sending [[United States Armed Forces|forces]] amidst invasion fears. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cjrzjqg8dlwt?page=6 (BBC News)] [https://fortune.com/2026/01/21/trump-greenland-solution-crisis-tariff-threat-nato-mark-rutte-davos/ (''Fortune'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 South Korean martial law crisis#Aftermath|2024 South Korean martial law crisis]]
**A [[High courts of South Korea|high court]] in [[Seoul]], [[South Korea]], sentences former [[Prime Minister of South Korea|prime minister]] [[Han Duck-soo]] to 23 years in [[Korea Correctional Service|prison]] for being an [[accomplice]] in giving procedural legitimacy to the [[martial law]] decree during a [[Cabinet of Yoon Suk Yeol|cabinet]] meeting. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/south-korea-court-finds-ex-pm-han-duck-soo-guilty-key-action-insurrection-over-2026-01-21/ (Reuters)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jan/21/former-south-korea-pm-han-duck-soo-jailed-martial-law-insurrection (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Corruption in Malaysia]]
**The [[Malaysia]]n [[Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission|anti-corruption commission]] charges two former [[Malaysian Armed Forces|military]] chiefs and one of their wives with [[money laundering]], [[abuse of power]], and criminal [[breach of confidence|breach of trust]]. [https://apnews.com/article/malaysia-military-chiefs-corruption-c47789e197b53d941123ad89bc05a745 (AP)]
*[[Trial of Tetsuya Yamagami]]
**A [[Judicial system of Japan|district court]] in [[Nara (city)|Nara]], [[Japan]], sentences [[Tetsuya Yamagami]] to [[Life imprisonment in Japan|life in prison]] for [[Assassination of Shinzo Abe|assassinating]] former [[Prime Minister of Japan|prime minister]] [[Shinzo Abe]] in 2022. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/japan-court-rule-trial-man-charged-with-killing-ex-pm-abe-2026-01-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[War on drugs]]
**[[Europol]] announces an end to an operation against [[synthetic drug]] production and trafficking in [[Belgium]], the [[Czech Republic]], [[Germany]], [[Netherlands]], [[Poland]], and [[Spain]], resulting in the arrests of 85 people and the seizure of 1,000 metric tons of chemicals in 24 labs. [https://www.dw.com/en/europol-busts-massive-synthetic-drug-production-network/a-75595738 (DW)]
